content.text: No non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant exists anywhere in the agreement. Every prohibition running against the Company is either an exclusivity covenant (§ 6.1), a confidentiality covenant (§ 8.3), or boilerplate — none restricts solicitation or hiring of the other Party's personnel. This is the preferred outcome for us, so no redline is warranted.

input.quote: Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no employee non-solicitation, anti-poaching or no-hire covenant, so the Company (our client) is under no such restriction — this meets the preferred position (no non-solicit on Customer), not merely the fallback. I read all five sections (every paragraph, p0000–p0074) and searched "solicit", "employ or engage", "hire", "induce", "recruit", "personnel" and "shall not"; there are no responsive hits. Article 5, the planner's likely location, deals only with site management and each Party's General Manager liaison (p0035) and imposes no personnel restriction. The only restrictive covenants are the Article 6 exclusivity provisions: § 6.1 restrains the Company from participating in competing Deerskin projects during the term, and § 6.3 restrains HDI for two years post-term (p0042) — both are product/market exclusivity, not personnel solicitation, and § 6.3 runs in our favour. Section 10.2 mentions "employee" only in the independent-contractor disclaimer (p0061). No redline is proposed; the exclusivity covenant at § 6.1 is a separate commercial term outside this rule and is not flagged here. If HDI later proposes a non-solicit, we would accept only the fallback shape: mutual, limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertisement and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.
